 Alexandra Eala, Bianca Andreescu and Zheng Qinwen among nominees for 2026 WTA Awards
 Originally posted on
 TennisUpToDate.com 
 By Cristhián Avila
  | 
 Last updated Nov 20, 2026 1:29 PM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
  The 2026 WTA season produced a number of significant breakthroughs, major title runs and remarkable comebacks. With the campaign now complete, the tour has announced the nominees for its annual player awards, recognising the competitors who made the biggest impact across the year.  
 The Player of the Year shortlist features five of the leading names in women's tennis, including world No. 1 Elena Rybakina and two-time Grand Slam champion Mirra Andreeva. Elsewhere, Alexandra Eala has been recognised for her progress, while Bianca Andreescu and Zheng Qinwen are among the candidates for Comeback Player of the Year.
 There are also opportunities for several younger players to receive recognition after making their mark on the WTA Tour . The Newcomer of the Year category includes five players who enjoyed important breakthroughs, while the doubles nominations reflect the success of some of the most consistent partnerships of the season.
 The winners will be announced during the week of December 14. Members of the media will decide the awards, while the WTA has also opened separate polls allowing fans to vote for their preferred players.
 Complete list of 2026 WTA Awards nominees
 The Player of the Year category is led by Rybakina, who enjoyed the most successful season of her career. The Kazakh won four titles, including the Australian Open and US Open, and finished the year at the top of the WTA rankings for the first time.

 Andreeva is another leading contender after capturing her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros and adding the WTA Finals trophy. The Russian ended the season as world No. 2, becoming the youngest player to finish a year in that position since Maria Sharapova in 2006.
 Sabalenka also had a highly productive campaign, winning three titles, including the Sunshine Double in Indian Wells and Miami. She recorded the most Grand Slam match wins of the season, with 19, and also led the tour in straight-set victories with 43.
 Svitolina's season was highlighted by titles in Rome and Auckland, as well as runs to the finals in Dubai and at the WTA Finals. Noskova, meanwhile, won two grass-court titles in Berlin and Wimbledon. Her run at the All England Club also contributed to the first all-Czech women's singles Grand Slam final.
 Doubles Team of the Year
 The Doubles Team of the Year category features five partnerships that enjoyed success across different stages of the season. Siniakova and Townsend headline the nominations after collecting six titles together, including two Grand Slam, three WTA 1000 and the WTA Finals.

 Dabrowski and Stefani also won six titles, including three WTA 1000 tournaments, and finished the season at the top of the doubles race. Krunic and Danilina reached the finals of the Australian Open, Indian Wells and Roland Garros, while also winning the Doha WTA 1000 event.
 Mladenovic and Guo made an immediate impact after joining forces this year, winning titles in Auckland and at Wimbledon. Errani and Paolini complete the shortlist after winning in Tokyo and reaching the finals in Miami and at the WTA Finals.
 Most Improved Player
 The Most Improved Player of the Year category includes five competitors who made significant progress during the 2026 campaign. Eala is among the nominees after establishing herself as a regular presence in the upper section of the rankings.

 Eala's season included her first WTA title in Washington and a run to the final in Hong Kong. She also reached the fourth round at Wimbledon, defeating defending champion Iga Swiatek, and recorded seven victories in 10 matches against top-10 opponents. Her rise to No. 15 marked another important step in her development.
 Kostyuk enjoyed one of the strongest seasons of her career, winning the Madrid WTA 1000 title and reaching the semifinals at both Roland Garros and Wimbledon. Shnaider also reached the French Open semifinals before claiming the Tokyo title, while Jovic continued her rapid progress with a successful title defence in Guadalajara and a final in Hobart.
 Cirstea completes the category after reaching the Roland Garros quarterfinals and the Rome semifinals. Her run in the Italian capital included a victory over then-world No. 1 Sabalenka, while she also won the title in Cluj and broke into the top 20 for the first time.
 Newcomer of the Year
 The Newcomer of the Year shortlist features five players who made notable advances on the professional circuit, with several already recording major results at WTA 500 and WTA 1000 level.

 Chwalinska's campaign stands out after she reached the Roland Garros final as a qualifier and subsequently won the Wuhan WTA 1000 title. She also recorded 11 victories against top-50 opponents, including her first top-10 win against Swiatek.

 Bejlek claimed the biggest title of her career in Abu Dhabi, winning a WTA 500 event, and later reached the semifinals in Cincinnati. Bartunkova, meanwhile, enjoyed an impressive first full season on tour, climbing from No. 126 to a career-high No. 29 and reaching the third round at the Australian Open, Wimbledon and US Open.
 Tagger won the Prague title and reached the final in Guangzhou, while making the main draw at all four Grand Slam tournaments. Gibson also made progress, reaching the final in Singapore and the quarterfinals in Osaka, Nottingham and Indian Wells.
 Andreescu and Zheng among comeback nominees
 The Comeback Player of the Year category includes five players who overcame significant interruptions to their careers or seasons. Andreescu and Zheng are arguably the most prominent names on the list, having both returned to a high level after difficult periods.

 Comeback Player of the Year nominee

 Zheng played only one tour-level tournament between July 2025 and February 2026 as she recovered from elbow surgery. After returning in Doha, she gradually rebuilt her form before producing one of the standout runs of the second half of the season.
 The Chinese player reached the US Open quarterfinals as a qualifier, extending a seven-match winning streak during that period, before claiming the Beijing WTA 1000 title. Her victory over Andreeva in the final secured her first trophy since Tokyo in 2024 and confirmed her return among the tour's leading players.
 Andreescu's comeback followed a different route. The former US Open champion began the year outside the top 200 but rebuilt her ranking through consistent performances on the WTA 125 circuit. She reached five finals, won titles in Sopo, Rovereto and Queretaro, and ended the season at No. 77.
 Kartal also made an encouraging return after spending six months away from competition because of a back injury. She came back in October and reached the Wuhan WTA 1000 final despite entering the tournament ranked No. 170.
 Pliskova returned at the Australian Open after missing almost all of the previous season with a left ankle injury. She later reached the semifinals in Nottingham and the quarterfinals in Linz, Madrid and Queen's. Podoroska, meanwhile, returned in March following a 14-month absence and won two World Tennis Tour titles before reaching her first WTA Tour final in Sao Paulo.
 With five categories covering singles, doubles, emerging talent and successful returns from injury, the 2026 nominees reflect the different stories that shaped the season.
 The winners will be announced during the week of December 14, when the WTA recognises the players whose performances left the strongest impression over the past year.
